findings.summary: Supports the continuous full-Theorem-9 converse for the stated reflected binary receiver pair, establishing C_sum ≤ 0.369296945969202842443 through an exact nonnegative six-row dual combination, continuum-wide interval majorants, and analytic maximization over all input priors.

Supports that, for 0 ≤ epsilon ≤ 1/3, the frontier six-row functional has an exactly equal nonnegative skew-invariant six-row representation for every prior, receiver pair, and admissible three-group hierarchy; this is an identity of functionals, not a proof that invariant duals are globally sufficient.

Qualifies the identification of the invariant functional with the named rank-eight quotient coordinates: the encoded mapping is algebraically consistent, but the supplied evidence does not independently reproduce the full quotient theorem or derive the map from all 15 skew-paired rows.

Supports, only for the specified frozen rounded slope and contact construction, that the earlier zero-intercept group-b line is infeasible and that an intercept of 10^-33 repairs the directed gap; it does not show that every possible zero-intercept supporting line is infeasible.

The assessment cannot determine the exact private-message sum-capacity or the global auxiliary optimization. The transaction certifies only one fixed reflected binary pair and does not establish global binary or reflected-pair sufficiency, dual or receiver-pair optimality, matching achievability, or the validity of the smaller numerical lead 0.369296340638082.
